notes: Science Report (Chen, Wu, Lin, Tan 1999); the PDF pages also carry fragments of the preceding (superconductivity STM) and following (NMDA receptor) Science reports, which were ignored. I1: uptake is gravimetric (TGA in a flowing H2 stream). The authors interpret the uptake as dissociative hydrogenation of the carbon (FTIR), but a gravimetric uptake value is measured, so the I1 exclusion for hydrogenation without measured uptake does not apply. Several values come from temperature-programmed TGA runs (e.g. 14.5 wt% at 673 K during reheating), i.e. temperature-cycle rather than isothermal; the 20 wt% (653 K, 2 h hold) and ~14 wt% (K-doped CNT, room temperature/298 K, 2 h hold) values are at stated T and ambient pressure (Table 1: 1 atm). TPD was used only to confirm desorption. I2: sorbents are Li- and K-doped multiwalled CNTs (and doped graphite); 'The Li/C and K/C ratio of these alkali-doped carbon materials was about 1/15 as measured by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy' (p. 91), which implies carbon is the majority by mass (about 96% for Li-doped, about 82% for K-doped). I4: the 130 m2/g (CNT) and 8.6 m2/g (graphite, Merck) areas, method unstated, refer to the undoped parent materials; the undoped CNT is itself measured in the paper (Fig. 2a FTIR; Table 1 CNT row 0.4 wt%), and the doped samples' areas would be area_same_sample = parent_material. The 0.4 wt%/no-uptake values for undoped CNT/graphite are attributed to ref. 9, but the doped-sample values are not stated to be previously published, so duplicate_data does not apply. is_retracted is false and the PDF has no retraction notice. No supplementary files were provided.
